Title: [FEATURE] --update should re-resolve transitive dependency tree when content changes at the same commit
Body: **Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

When a package author updates the dependency tree (e.g. removes a transitive dependency) without creating a new commit on the default branch, `apm install --update` does not detect the change. It compares the `resolved_commit` in `apm.lock.yaml` against the current upstream ref — and since the commit SHA is identical, it skips re-resolution entirely. The only workaround is to delete `apm.lock.yaml` and run a fresh `apm install`.

Title: Content security scanning for prompt files (hidden Unicode detection)
Body: ## Problem

Shared prompt and instruction files (`.cursorrules`, `.github/prompts/`, etc.) are becoming a de facto supply chain — but without any integrity guarantees. Researchers [found that 6 of 50 popular shared `.cursorrules` files](https://agentseal.org/blog/cursor-rules-hidden-instructions) contained hidden zero-width Unicode characters embedded between visible text.

These characters are invisible to humans but LLMs tokenize them individually, meaning models can process instructions developers cannot see. Some had patterns consistent with deliberate instruction embedding using Unicode tag characters (U+E0001–U+E007F), which map 1:1 to invisible
[Middle omitted to fit model context]
 |

### Product positioning

This is the first pillar of `apm audit`. Future modes include `--ci` (lock consistency) and `--drift` (on-disk divergence), as documented in the [governance guide](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/enterprise/governance/).

Title: [BUG] Codex adapter writes ${VAR} MCP header values into static http_headers
Body: **Describe the bug**

The Codex client adapter writes an MCP server's `headers` into `~/.codex/config.toml` as `http_headers` with any `${VAR}` placeholder copied verbatim. Codex documents `http_headers` as a map of header names to **static values**; environment-sourced values go through `env_http_headers` (header name → environment variable name) or `bearer_token_env_var`. The adapter never emits either of those, so a remote MCP server whose header references an environment variable is configured for Codex with the unexpanded
[Middle omitted to fit model context]
 the HTTP request Codex sends. The report rests on the written `config.toml`, the adapter source, and Codex's documented field semantics. Claude Code's adapter writes the identical placeholder into `headers`, where Claude Code documents environment-variable expansion, so the same dependency resolves the variable for one target and not the other.

Title: Expose `apm-version` as an import input on `shared/apm.md`

The shared workflow pins the apm CLI version only through `microsoft/apm-action`'s built-in default — it does not expose `apm-version` as an import input. To run a newer apm CLI than the action's default, a consumer must **hand-edit the vendored `shared/apm.md`** (the `apm-version`
[Middle omitted to fit model context]
 `uses:` ref at compile time), so bumping the *action* still means editing the vendored file or pulling a newer upstream `shared/apm.md`. Exposing `apm-version` covers the common case — a newer CLI on the existing action — without that edit, since the action accepts the input regardless.

Title: Deprecate and remove `apm marketplace publish` (consumer-repo fan-out)
Body: ## Why

`apm marketplace publish` opens branches and PRs against a list of downstream consumer repositories (`consumer-targets.yml`) to bump their pin to a newly published marketplace version. This is **out of scope for a package manager**:

- npm, pip, cargo, brew, gem, go, composer - none of them update downstream consumers. Producers publish; consumers pull on their own cadence.
- Consumer-repo fan-out is **CI / Renovate / Dependabot territory**. Those tools already do this better, with policy controls, batching, scheduling, security review, and a maintained ecosystem.
